A quieter way to read

Reading a long article should be a calm experience. Local tools can help readers collect useful information without sending their working notes to a remote service. An extracted article becomes a starting point that the reader can inspect and correct before using it for any further task.

A good extraction keeps the author's paragraphs, headings, and meaningful tables together. It removes navigation menus and repeated subscription prompts so that the main argument is easier to follow. Even a careful algorithm can miss a caption or keep an unwanted sentence, which is why an editable preview matters.

The reader stays in control

Readers can correct a name, add missing context, or remove a section that does not belong in their notes. Unicode text such as café, বাংলা, and naïve should survive the journey from the original page to the editor. Paragraph breaks should remain visible so that editing does not become a chore.

Once the text has been reviewed, it can serve as the input for a later summary. For now, fetching and editing provide a small but complete first step. Keeping this process on the reader's own device makes it possible to understand exactly which words are being prepared for the next stage.
